plan: [I correct for the winner’s curse in this common‑value, second‑price auction. Given my signal 23 the prior on the common value is flat, but being the highest signal makes lower common values more likely. Calculating E[V | my signal=23 and I’m highest] ≈ 23.78. I’ll round to the nearest $0.1.]

[I will avoid the winner’s curse by bidding my posterior expected common value given my signal 45. With common C uniform 20–29 and noise uniform -20–20, feasible C values are 25–29, equally likely. The posterior mean is (25+26+27+28+29)/5 = 27. In a second-price auction bidding this expectation maximizes my long-run profit.]

[My signal is 6. Prior common value is uniform 20–29 and noise is uniform −20–20, so feasible common values given my signal are 20–26, giving E[common | signal=6] = (20+26)/2 = 23. In a second-price auction with interdependent values, bidding my posterior expected common value is the appropriate Bayes strategy to maximize expected profit while avoiding the winner’s curse. I will therefore bid my posterior mean: $23.00.]
